entry.summary: Adversarial Robustness Is Not Zero-Day Generalization: A Controlled Evaluation of Flow-Based Intrusion Detectors on Corrected CIC-IDS2017 arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper tests whether synthetic variants of known attacks can stand in for unseen (zero-day) attacks when evaluating machine-learning network intrusion detectors. On the corrected CIC-IDS2017 dataset, four models were compared on detection under constrained perturbations of known attacks and on detection when an entire attack family is held out of training. Detection was consistently much higher under perturbation than on held-out families, so the authors conclude the two measures should be reported separately. ★★★★ Notable: The authors test whether adversarial perturbations proxy zero-day attacks, reporting large gaps versus leave-one-family-out detection across four models.

entry.title: Learning timeline-preserving speech-to-speech translation
entry.summary: Learning Timeline-Preserving Speech-to-Speech Translation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes timeline-preserving speech-to-speech translation, which requires translated speech and pauses to align with the source speech on a shared absolute timeline. The authors present TransDubber, an end-to-end system trained on 642K duration-matched English-Chinese speech pairs, using progressive supervised training combined with verifier-guided reinforcement learning. On a 4,353-utterance test set, compared with UniSS, the share of translations within 2% of the source duration rises from 25.6% to 61.5%, and pause-alignment F1 rises from 0.118 to 0.550, while translation quality stays competitive. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formulate timeline-preserving S2ST, build 642K duration-matched pairs, and report large gains in duration and pause alignment over UniSS on 4,353 utterances.

entry.title: Governing Human-Agent Software Teams Through Message Protocols
entry.summary: Getting a Grip: Operating Human-Agent Software Teams Through Governed Messages arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proposes governing teams of humans and coding agents through their message protocol, introducing yoars, a relay where authenticated participants exchange typed, addressed messages in rooms with goals, decision rules, and an append-only record. In 926 controlled runs with small agent teams, revising which messages start work and limiting repeated messages reduced total coordination failure from 42% to 13%. Instructed roles and votes did not reliably produce the intended process, and in-conversation defenses did not reliably prevent a planted backdoor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose governing human-agent software teams via a message protocol, reporting controlled runs and a four-week field study.

entry.title: Graph foundation model built from a frozen time-series model via parallel paths
entry.summary: Versatile Graph Foundation Models from Frozen Time-Series Foundation Models via Parallel Flows arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes GraphFlowFM, which uses a frozen time-series foundation model (TimesFM) as a graph foundation model, without graph pre-training or gradient updates on the target graph. The method splits a graph into parallel flows, vertex-disjoint paths that together cover every edge, and treats each path as a multivariate time series whose time steps are nodes. A causal-attention encoder and a closed-form ridge readout weigh each node's tokens by their alignment with the labels. The authors report the best average rank on 21 node-classification datasets and superior link-prediction results on all six datasets compared with pre-trained graph foundation models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors repurpose a frozen time-series foundation model for graphs via parallel flows, reporting leading node classification across 21 datasets without graph pre-training.

entry.title: Cyclotomic polynomials whose irreducible factors over finite fields have three terms
entry.summary: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper classifies pairs (q,n), where q is a prime power and gcd(n,q)=1 with n>1, for which every irreducible factor of the cyclotomic polynomial Φ_n(x) over F_q has exactly three nonzero terms. The greatest common divisor of the positive support exponents yields a unique reduction by a power substitution. The paper gives the corresponding arithmetic conditions and explicit factorizations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors classify pairs (q,n) for which all irreducible factors of cyclotomic polynomials over finite fields are trinomials, via power substitution reduction.

entry.title: Linking Singular Learning Theory and Mechanistic Interpretability in Billion-Parameter Models
entry.summary: Bridging Singular Learning Theory and Mechanistic Interpretability at the Billion-Parameter Scale arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper connects two ways of describing trained neural networks: mechanistic interpretability, which finds components that implement a computation, and singular learning theory, which measures the geometry of the loss. The authors test this link in the Pythia-1B language model on a Dyck bracket-matching task across 154 training checkpoints, comparing against a five-stage circuit identified through interventions. They find that changes in the Fisher trace track changes in causal effect, with a median partial rank correlation of 0.51. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify singular learning theory and mechanistic interpretability via one parameter-to-prediction map, testing it on Pythia-1B across 154 checkpoints.

entry.title: LDST: Tuning Mixed Integer Programming Solvers Using Solver Log Analysis
entry.summary: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), a method that uses a large language model to read solver logs and propose sparse edits to the current best configuration, validating each before execution. It selects tuning signals adaptively based on what a time-limited run reveals and estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduced geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose LLM-driven tuning of MIP solvers from logs, reporting 43.9% and 16.7% loss reductions over SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search on 215 instances.

entry.title: Compressed Oracle Duality: a framework for what quantum adversaries know
entry.summary: Compressed Oracle Duality: A simple framework for knowing what quantum adversaries know arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to characterize the information a quantum adversary querying a random oracle retains. It proposes "Compressed Oracle Duality," which extends the Compressed Oracle method to space-bounded algorithms by applying an isometry to the adversary's memory, yielding two compressed oracles with identical marginals. The framework is applied to collision search, giving a simplified proof of a recent quantum time-space tradeoff for label-symmetric algorithms and a stronger classical tradeoff under label symmetry. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a compressed oracle duality framework for space-bounded adversaries and apply it to collision search time-space tradeoffs.

entry.title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Finding Access Control Flaws in Android Firmware
entry.summary: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper points out that existing tools flag dangerous behavior only when an app calls a predefined set of sensitive APIs, missing vulnerabilities where a generic API, such as a database read, operates on protected data without adequate access control. The authors present Callix, which judges how sensitive each callsite is by analyzing both the API's function and the data it handles, recovers each security check as an explicit property, and uses a restriction context to decide whether those checks suffice. Evaluated on 1,750 pre-installed apps from ten top Android vendors, Callix found 819 vulnerable paths, 42.1% of which allow reading or modifying private user data through generic database operations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors combine callsite sensitivity with access-control sufficiency analysis; they report 819 vulnerable paths across 1,750 pre-installed apps from 10 vendors, with 95.1% precision.

entry.title: Beyond price: analyzing economic-state manipulation flaws in DeFi
entry.summary: Price is Only the Symptom: Understanding and Analyzing Economic-State Manipulation Vulnerabilities in DeFi arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper empirically studies economic-state manipulation (ESM) vulnerabilities in decentralized finance, using 276 real-world attacks and 91 Code4rena audit findings. It proposes a cause-oriented taxonomy with four primary categories and eleven subcategories. The authors find these vulnerabilities often involve violations of protocol accounting, AMM state consistency, and execution-time constraints, not just price manipulation. Among seven evaluated detection approaches, the best identified only 50.4% of real-world attacks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a cause-oriented taxonomy of economic-state manipulation, evaluated on 276 real attacks and 91 audit findings across seven detection approaches.

entry.title: Conic programming method to certify Transformer attention robustness
entry.summary: Conic Certification of Transformer Attention arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to certify, with guarantees, how much an attention head's output in large language models can change under input perturbations. The authors develop a conic programming theory and show that the difficulty stems from the bilinear interaction between a varying query and the keys rather than from the softmax. They propose an exponential cone moment relaxation and report computational results on GPT-2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formulate attention certification as conic programming, prove NP-hardness from query-key bilinearity, and report a quadratic error bound with tighter GPT-2 results than linear bound propag

entry.title: Budget-limited risk monitoring: how free input covariates speed detection
entry.summary: The First-Order Value of Free Covariates in Budgeted Risk Monitoring arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies how to spend a limited label budget to detect rising risk in a deployed model quickly while controlling false alarms. It proves that rules choosing label requests only from their own label history have worst-case detection delay of at least (1/h(r)+1/c)log A to first order, where h(r) is the Bernoulli KL divergence between the changed risk and the threshold. When a harmful change also shifts inputs, a rule letting inputs trigger labeling attains delay log A/h(r) on a Gaussian model, with synthetic and ACS experiments. A benign input shift, however, can cause the covariate trigger to request nearly every label. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a first-order delay lower bound for label-history rules and quantify rounds saved by free covariates, checked on synthetic and two ACS tasks.

entry.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast, principled method for generating training data for AI reasoning
entry.summary: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes SFTProbe, which predicts the difficulty and diversity of reasoning training data directly instead of generating large pools and then filtering them. It uses brief LoRA-based adaptation and evaluates loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace. The authors report that data curation drops from weeks to hours, and that 5k generated math examples match an 89k filtered dataset. Code and data are released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors probe the loss basin with low-rank LoRA perturbations to predict reasoning data quality, validated on math and physics tasks.

entry.title: Proof that exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models is FIXP-complete
entry.summary: FIXP-Completeness in Second-Price Auctions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proves that computing exact equilibria is FIXP-complete in three second-price auction models: return-on-investment pacing with a multiplier cap of 1+δ, budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping, and budget-constrained throttling. The proofs rely on a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem built from clipped affine gates and a reciprocal gate. The results address open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a generalized-circuit FIXP-complete basis and report FIXP-completeness for three second-price auction equilibrium problems in automated bidding.

entry.title: Designing LLM-generated heuristics that stay robust by optimizing tail risk, not just averages
entry.summary: Robustness Starts with the Objective: Designing and Certifying Robust LLM-Generated Heuristics arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents TAILOR, a framework that uses large language models to design computer-system heuristics while optimizing the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of cost differences against an existing baseline. It was evaluated on three case studies (Azure GPU batch admission, Azure VM packing, and server placement) and seven optimization benchmarks. The authors report that on six of the benchmarks, the resulting heuristics are certified with 99% confidence to improve both average performance and tail optimality gaps over the baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose paired CVaR as an LLM heuristic synthesis objective, prove improvement guarantees without computing the optimum, and report evaluation on three case studies and seven benchmarks.

entry.title: Swapping, Replicating and Reading Probability Mass: An Auditing Protocol for Demographic Bias in Direct-Answer AI Models
entry.summary: Swap, Replicate, Read the Mass: A Protocol for Auditing Demographic Bias in System One Decision Models arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a protocol for auditing demographic bias in "System One" decision models, which return typed, probability-scored answers instead of free text. The authors adapt three benchmarks (BBQ, CrowS-Pairs, SilverSpoon) and run 1,638,000 decisions across twelve models and a no-thinking ablation, swapping option order and repeating runs under different seeds. They report widespread stereotype alignment, answers that depend on option order, and confidence scores that track instability more than bias. The authors recommend that audits permute options and reverse questions by default, and that order-invariant scoring become a procurement requirement. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt BBQ, CrowS-Pairs, and SilverSpoon to typed interfaces and report 1.638M decisions across twelve models, with option swaps revealing order dependence and stereotype alignment.

entry.title: Single-shot state preparation threshold: a rigorous theorem and statistical mechanical mapping
entry.summary: Single-shot state preparation thresholds in quantum LDPC codes: soundness, confinement, and statistical mechanics arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper studies the threshold for preparing logical codewords using one round of noisy syndrome measurements, called single-shot state preparation. The authors prove that for CSS quantum LDPC codes with at least logarithmic distance, linear confinement alone guarantees a nonzero threshold, and under linear soundness the residual data error is local stochastic. entry.title: Undirected network coding enables faster external-memory integer sorting
entry.summary: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting arXiv · Oct 14, 2026The paper gives a finite counterexample showing that, in undirected networks, network coding and fractional routing can achieve different rate combinations, contrary to the multiple-unicast conjecture. Using the counterexample's linear structure, it proposes a deterministic external-memory integer sorting algorithm whose block-transfer count is asymptotically smaller than the classical comparison-sorting bound in some parameter ranges. The algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound are formally verified in Lean. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a finite counterexample to the multiple-unicast conjecture and use its linear structure to obtain a deterministic external-memory integer sort whose I/O bound is asymptotically smalle

entry.title: Pricing Buyers Using Features of Differing Trustworthiness
entry.summary: SALE: Source-Aware Dynamic Pricing with Strategic Buyers arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper proposes a source-aware framework for contextual dynamic pricing, distinguishing verified customer features from self-reported ones that buyers may manipulate. The SALE policy uses verified features to localize price exploration and combines both feature types during exploitation to correct strategic manipulation. The authors establish consistent sparse estimation and a sublinear expected regret bound in a high-dimensional semiparametric setting, supported by simulations and real-data experiments. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes SALE, a source-aware dynamic pricing framework for strategic buyers, with sublinear regret and uniform noise-distribution estimation guarantees in high dimensions.

entry.title: Beyond Light Cones: Complexity of Preparing States for Quantum Spin Glasses
entry.summary: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses arXiv · Oct 2, 2026This paper introduces a method for studying how hard it is to prepare states of dense quantum p-spin Hamiltonians, going beyond limits based only on circuit light cones. It uses an effective profile complexity derived from Pauli profiles. The authors show that near-ground-state energy requires Ω(n²/log n) one- and two-qubit gates, and they give depth-width, entanglement and matrix product state lower bounds. ★★★★ Notable: Combines a nonsymmetric quantum de Finetti theorem with Gaussian process entropy bounds to go beyond lightcone limits, reporting Omega(n^2/log n) gate lower bounds and magic-hierarchy obstructions.

entry.title: A Tale of Two Walks: Linking Kac's Quantum Random Walk to the KMP Process
entry.summary: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper shows that the parallel Kac walk's twirling channel on the symmetric subspace is exactly encoded by a classical Markov chain on partitions, which lifts to a parallel KMP process on complete graphs. The authors prove that O(log d + log(1/ε)) repetitions approximate Haar twirling to error ε, uniformly in the number of copies t. They also give a mixing-time bound for standard KMP on general graphs and apply it to improve coordinate hit-and-run mixing on the simplex. ★★★★ Notable: Reveals a new link between parallel Kac walk and KMP; the authors report Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace approximated in repetitions independent of t, and improve simplex coordinate hit-and-ru

entry.title: Secret sharing without extractable randomness: a negative answer to Bosley–Dodis
entry.summary: Secret Sharing Despite Non-Extractable Randomness IACR ePrint · Oct 14, 2026This cryptography preprint asks whether two-out-of-two secret sharing requires randomness sources from which nearly uniform bits can be deterministically extracted. The authors construct a class of flat sources and a perfectly correct, perfectly private scheme that splits a b-bit secret into two (b+1)-bit shares. They show that every deterministic function is far from uniform on some source in the class, answering the Bosley–Dodis question in the negative. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that two-out-of-two secret sharing can be perfect over non-extractable sources, answering the Bosley–Dodis open question negatively via a parity argument, and extend the idea to two-o

entry.title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Generative Recommendation
entry.summary: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the cold-start problem of recommending creators a user does not yet follow, arguing that the Semantic ID layer used in generative recommenders, not the language model, is the main bottleneck. The authors propose Atomic Creator Token (ACT), which gives each creator its own vocabulary token trained end-to-end, avoiding SID collisions and blocked gradients. In a controlled comparison on production data, ACT outperforms a matched SID baseline on creator-level Recall@15, and it also leads on the public KuaiRand dataset. A live A/B test shows directionally positive results on every reported metric. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose per-creator atomic tokens trained end-to-end, comparing against semantic IDs on production data and KuaiRand, plus a live A/B test.

entry.title: SCRAMJet: An Ultra-Low-Latency Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger
entry.summary: SCRAMJet: An Ultra Low Latency JetClass-Scale Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger arXiv · Oct 21, 2026This paper presents SCRAMJet, a transformer encoder for Level-1 triggers at the High-Luminosity LHC that replaces multi-head attention with a low-rank projection and uses per-parameter learned fixed-point quantization. It is compiled to Verilog for FPGA implementation and is evaluated on the ten-class JetClass dataset, where it meets timing on a Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P at 147 ns. The authors also report that resource-aware training can silently remove attention channels from the compiled circuit, and that a floor on the attention datalane prevents this. ★★★★ Notable: Replaces multi-head attention with low-rank projection plus learned quantization and Verilog compilation; the authors report JetClass results and a virtual-channel effect.

entry.title: Faces or Models? Where Age Gaps in Expression Recognition Come From
entry.summary: Faces or Models? Where the Age Gap in Facial Expression Recognition Comes From arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This study tested five open-source facial expression recognition models on the FACES database, which contains 2,052 posed photos of 171 adults aged 19 to 80. Every model was less accurate on older faces, by 11.7 to 15.2 percentage points, and human raters also performed worse on them. Retraining only the final classification layer on older faces shrank the gap to 4 points or less, suggesting the models' features can represent older faces and the problem lies in how the final layer was trained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate facial aging from model training, comparing five FER models with human and geometry baselines on 2,052 photos, reporting the gap shrinks after refitting only the final layer.

entry.title: Early fault-tolerant magic state generation using color codes on a superconducting processor
entry.summary: Early Fault-Tolerant Magic State Synthesis and Spacetime Efficient Analog Rotations with Color Code on a Superconducting Quantum Processor arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper reports the first implementations of two magic state generation methods on a superconducting quantum processor using the color code: STAR for near-term computing and fault-tolerant magic state synthesis for long-term computing. The authors present a STAR-type injection protocol on the color code and build an MSS factory from multi-patch magic state cultivation, interleaved transversal Clifford operations, and lattice-surgery teleportation. Fidelity results under post-selection are reported, and post-selection, most-likely-error, and concatenated-matching decoding are compared. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first superconducting-processor implementations of STAR injection and multi-patch cultivation on the color code, reaching about 91% logical magic state fidelity.

entry.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
entry.summary: Triple descent in quantum linear regression arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies prediction error in quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, when features are estimated from finitely many measurement shots. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the error shows a triple-descent profile with two peaks of different origins. A classical peak arises when the measurement first becomes informationally complete and can be suppressed by more shots at inference. A quantum peak appears when outcomes match training states and cannot be removed by more shots. Using random-matrix theory, the authors derive both peak shapes analytically, including ridge regularization. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a second, quantum peak from finite-shot noise in quantum linear regression, derived analytically via random-matrix theory including ridge regularization.

entry.title: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for symmetric Werner states
entry.summary: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper exactly computes the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification for normalized symmetric Werner states in every local dimension d≥2, giving a closed-form expression. The authors prove additivity for tensor powers and for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. They show that the canonical purification and its products achieve these values even when arbitrary joint purifications with finite-dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. The paper also proves continuity of the optimal value at the symmetric endpoint under perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an exact closed form for the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of symmetric Werner states, with additivity and global optimality results.

entry.title: Study of expected shortfall estimation and capital coverage using overlapping scenarios
entry.summary: Expected shortfall estimation and capital coverage under overlapping scenarios arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how estimating expected shortfall (ES) from short profit-and-loss samples built from overlapping multi-day returns affects accuracy and capital coverage. It compares six order-statistic-based ES estimators, using a one-year window and 2.5% confidence level as a benchmark, with both simulations and market data. The authors find that overlapping sampling systematically shifts ES estimates downward, weakening capital coverage, with serial dependence and heavy tails amplifying the effect. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link overlapping multi-day return samples to ES estimator mismatch and quantify effects on capital coverage, reporting simulations and market data on twelve risk factors and ninety-nine po

entry.title: Learning dynamics by matching velocities: a simulation-free training method for nonlinear systems
entry.summary: Learning to evolve by matching velocities arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how to learn the continuous-time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems. The authors propose Velocity Matching (VM), a training objective that avoids simulating trajectories and backpropagating through numerical solvers. They develop stability estimates that control trajectory errors through velocity errors. In numerical experiments on nonlinear ODEs and semi-discretized time-dependent PDEs, VM is reported to be more accurate than trajectory-based objectives. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose simulation-free Velocity Matching, with stability and universal approximation theory linking it to A-stable Runge-Kutta schemes; reported gains on ODEs and semi-discretized PDEs.

entry.title: Statistical inference when predictions shape the data they learn from
entry.summary: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies performativity, where prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, as in policy-making and self-evolving AI systems. The authors build an end-to-end statistical inference framework, deriving central limit theorems and covariance recursions for repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent. They propose consistent covariance estimators based on policy perturbations and score matching, and extend prediction-powered inference to this setting. Experiments show that ignoring propagated uncertainty can cause substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend statistical inference to performative repeated risk minimization and gradient descent, deriving covariance recursions and prediction-powered inference, evaluated on synthetic and LL

entry.title: Online fair division of chores with upgrade recourse
entry.summary: Online Fair Division of Chores with Upgrade Recourse arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies online fair division of indivisible chores among n agents, where earlier assignments may be revised but each previously assigned chore must be replaced by a different chore the agent finds no more costly. The authors show that a simple adaptation of round robin achieves envy-freeness up to one chore (EF1) together with a (2-1/n)-approximation of the maximin share (MMS). They also prove that no deterministic algorithm without predictions can do better on this MMS factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a round-robin adaptation achieving EF1 and (2-1/n)-MMS under upgrade recourse, plus a matching deterministic lower bound and prediction-based improvements.

entry.title: VESPER: Learning Free-Energy Landscapes Online with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective
entry.summary: VESPER: Online Learning of Free Energies with a Multi-Tempered Variational Objective arXiv · Oct 31, 2026VESPER is a method that learns free-energy landscapes over collective variables while molecular dynamics simulations run. The evolving model biases the simulations to cross energy barriers more easily, and data from several tempering levels train one shared model without reweighting. The authors prove conditional convergence of the coupled dynamics and test the method on alanine dipeptide, alanine tetrapeptide, methane dehydrogenation on Ni(511), and chignolin. ★★★★ Notable: The authors couple enhanced sampling with neural free-energy learning via one convex variational objective over multiple tempering levels, reporting tests on alanine peptides, methane dehydrogenation,

entry.title: Two strategies for drawing conclusions: shaping representations versus reasoning in context
entry.summary: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper formalizes two inference strategies: a geometric strategy that gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect relational structure, making later inference cheap, and an algebraic strategy that flexibly reasons over novel relations given in context at extra computational cost. The authors identify opposing signatures of these strategies in transitive inference. Experiments with humans, neural networks trained from scratch, and large language models demonstrate these effects. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize geometric and algebraic inference and report opposing signatures in transitive inference across humans, trained networks, and LLMs, with causal interventions.
